tutorial.overviewTitle: Tutorial: Using a Crochet Hook to Pick Up Dropped Stitch
overviewSteps: Insert your crochet hook into the dropped stitch.
Find the strand that connects the stitches in the row above.
Grab the strand with your crochet hook and pull the yarn through.
Repeat these steps until you used up all strands and you are back to your current row.
Slip the stitch back to your left needle.

steps.heading: Insert your crochet hook into the dropped stitch.

checklist.text: Your work should be facing you on the right side.
Make sure you didn't accidentally twist the stitch.
The loose strands should all be in the back of the dropped stitch.

steps.heading: Find the strand that connects the stitches in the row above.

checklist.text: Sometimes the strands twist around a bit. You need to catch the lowest one.

steps.heading: Grab the strand with your crochet hook and pull the yarn through.

checklist.text: The new stitch sits snugly, not too tight or loose

steps.heading: Repeat these steps until you used up all strands and you are back to your current row.

checklist.text: You're not skipping any bars as you go
The column of stitches stays aligned

steps.heading: Slip the stitch back to your left needle.

checklist.text: Make sure you don't accidentally twist it as you do.
